chains.title: ARID5B binds the ref-T allele of the FTO intronic enhancer; loss of binding on alt-C derepresses IRX3/IRX5 in subcutaneous preadipocytes and shifts adipogenesis toward white fat

links.claim: ARID5B binds the ref-T allele more strongly than the alt-C allele at rs1421085.
rs1421085 lies in an FTO intronic enhancer whose ARID5B-binding motif is disrupted by alt-C.
Loss of ARID5B occupancy on alt-C relieves repression and increases IRX3/IRX5 expression.
The enhancer is active and the effect occurs in subcutaneous adipose preadipocytes.
Higher IRX3/IRX5 biases adipocyte precursors toward white adipogenesis, contributing to obesity.

predictions: ARID5B binds the ref-T probe more strongly than the alt-C probe
alt-C increases enhancer reporter activity in preadipocytes
alt-C increases IRX3/IRX5 expression in subcutaneous preadipocytes
alt-C favors white adipogenesis and reduces browning capacity
falsified_if: ARID5B binding is not allele-specific at rs1421085 in preadipocyte extracts.
The alt-C enhancer reporter is not more active than ref-T in preadipocytes.
alt-C does not increase IRX3/IRX5 in preadipocytes.

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of rs1421085: the obesity association reflects a linked causal variant in LD or a passenger variant, with no allele-specific TF binding at this position
predictions: ARID5B binding is not allele-specific at rs1421085
The ref-T and alt-C enhancer reporters have equal activity in preadipocytes
IRX3/IRX5 and FTO are not allele-specifically expressed in preadipocytes
The obesity signal is attributable to a different variant in linkage disequilibrium
falsified_if: Allele-specific ARID5B binding and allele-specific enhancer activity are demonstrated in preadipocytes.
The alt-C allele reproducibly changes IRX3/IRX5 or FTO expression in the relevant cell type.

chains.title: ARID5B loss at the same FTO intronic enhancer directly changes FTO expression rather than IRX3/IRX5

links.claim: ARID5B binds the ref-T allele more strongly than the alt-C allele at rs1421085.
rs1421085 lies in an FTO intronic enhancer whose ARID5B motif is disrupted by alt-C.
The enhancer directly regulates FTO expression in cis.
The effect occurs in subcutaneous adipose preadipocytes.
Altered FTO dosage affects body-weight regulation and contributes to obesity.

predictions: ARID5B binds the ref-T probe more strongly than the alt-C probe
alt-C changes FTO expression in preadipocytes
IRX3/IRX5 expression is not allele-specifically changed in the same cells
falsified_if: FTO expression is not allele-specific in preadipocytes.
IRX3/IRX5, not FTO, is the allele-specific target of the enhancer.

chains.title: ARID5B loss at the FTO intronic enhancer acts on IRX3 in hypothalamic neurons to alter energy balance rather than in adipocytes

links.claim: ARID5B binds the ref-T allele more strongly than the alt-C allele at rs1421085.
rs1421085 lies in an FTO intronic enhancer whose ARID5B motif is disrupted by alt-C.
The relevant effect occurs in hypothalamic neurons.
Altered hypothalamic IRX3 changes appetite and energy balance, contributing to obesity.

predictions: ARID5B binding is stronger on ref-T than alt-C in hypothalamic cell extracts
alt-C increases IRX3 in hypothalamic neurons
IRX3/IRX5 is not allele-specifically changed in subcutaneous preadipocytes
falsified_if: ARID5B or IRX3 is not expressed in the relevant hypothalamic cells.
The allele-specific effect is present only in adipocytes and absent in hypothalamic models.

matrix.test: Allele-specific ARID5B binding at rs1421085 (EMSA or oligo pulldown with preadipocyte nuclear extract, ARID5B immunodepletion)

outcomes.outcome: ref-T binds ARID5B more strongly than alt-C

matrix.test: Allele-specific enhancer reporter activity in subcutaneous preadipocytes
Allele-specific IRX3/IRX5 expression in subcutaneous preadipocytes (e.g. ASE or CRISPR-edited isogenic lines)

outcomes.outcome: alt-C changes FTO dosage with no IRX3/IRX5 change

matrix.test: Allele-specific IRX3 in hypothalamic neurons (or hypothalamic-relevant model)

outcomes.outcome: allele-specific IRX3 change only in hypothalamic cells

next_experiment: Single cheapest decisive assay: an allele-specific enhancer reporter (ref-T vs alt-C fragment cloned upstream of a minimal promoter–luciferase, or an MPRA oligo containing rs1421085) transfected into subcutaneous preadipocytes or a preadipocyte line. It separates H1 (alt-C increases enhancer activity) from H0 (no allelic difference) and from H3 (effect requires hypothalamic, not adipose, context); a positive result then needs IRX3/IRX5 expression measurement to separate H1 from H2.
